```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

The package keeps descriptive fit, posterior predictive checks, prediction,
and predictive criteria separate because they answer different questions.

```{r}
library(VariationalBayesHLRM)
set.seed(301)
X <- cbind(intercept = 1, predictor = seq(-1.5, 1.5, length.out = 30))
data <- list(X = X, y = drop(X %*% c(0.5, 1.25)) + rnorm(30, sd = 0.4))
prior <- lrm_prior(c(0, 0), 10 * diag(2), 4, 1)
fit <- fit_model(
  lrm_model(2), data, prior, "cavi", initialization_ols(),
  cavi_control(max_iterations = 300, evaluation_draws = 100),
  seed = 302, verbose = FALSE
)

evaluate_in_sample_fit(fit)
check <- posterior_predictive_check(fit, n_draws = 100, seed = 303)
plot(check)

new_design <- X[c(1, 15, 30), , drop = FALSE]
predict(fit, new_design, n_draws = 100, seed = 304)
prediction <- posterior_predict(fit, new_design, n_draws = 100, seed = 305)
plot(prediction)

criteria <- predictive_criteria(
  fit, n_draws = 100, seed = 306,
  return_log_likelihood = TRUE
)
criteria$criteria$waic
dim(as_log_lik_matrix(criteria$log_likelihood$observation))
plot(criteria$log_likelihood$observation)
```

WAIC, PSIS-LOO, cross-validation, and held-out scores are comparable only when
their dataset, predictive unit, target, conditioning convention, and likelihood
match. PSIS-LOO is restricted to converged MCMC posterior draws; CAVI and SVI
use refitted cross-validation when leave-one-out evidence is required.
